_doc: Salt Creek Valley master plan, Phase 1 (planning only; Sean's brief of 2026-11-07, issue #467, PR #621's valley inputs). INERT: nothing in the game reads this file until Sean approves the geometry. The maps, profiles and tables are generated from it by tools/valley/valley_plan.py (never drawn by hand), so moving a point here moves it everywhere. Read with docs/briefs/valley-plan.md (the reasons, the DECIDED/PROPOSED/OPEN calls, the migration) and docs/briefs/valley-tables.md (generated: the coordinate schedule, travel times, grades, checks).

status_words.DECIDED: Sean's; not reopened without asking him.
status_words.PROPOSED: this plan's recommendation; a working value, never canon until Sean says so.

envelope._doc: 4.4 x 3.6 km, 15.8 km2 (the DECIDED 'about 4 x 4 km' area). The town sits west of the middle, near the base of the western foothills (DECIDED, valley.md); the east holds the canyon, the trestle, the overpass and the widow; the south the open homestead and ranch country. Selective boundaries, never a wall of cliffs all round.

boundaries.how: the La Plata front: the foothills steepen past x -2000 into timbered slopes and broken mesas (climbable a little way, then too steep for a horse); the rail goes into its tunnel there.
past z -1400 the arroyo's headwater ridges and broken mesa country; the timber thins out; scenery beyond.

Salt Creek leaves through a narrowing gorge at the north-east (too rough to follow far); the rail leaves in a rock cut; the east road runs on toward Durango as a track whose far end is distance and the land's fold, not a wall.
rimrock mesas and broken canyon country (the outlaw hideout's mesa); the Baron's range continues off the map behind his fence line.

scenery.what: the La Plata Mountains, NW to W, about 20-30 km off, about 4,000 m (real)
the sunset notch: a low saddle in the western skyline due west of Main Street (bearing 270), kept clear of the rail line, which leaves 12 degrees north of it
the San Juan peaks and mesas, far north and north-east
Mesa country falling away south toward the San Juan River

speeds._doc: Travel times use these. The player's are the game's (config/movement/middle.tres). The horse isn't ridden yet (#341, #478): its gaits are PROPOSED from period horse numbers.

terrain._doc: How the generator makes the ground (the same function will bake Phase 2's height map): (1) a smooth surface through the control points [x, z, y] (thin-plate spline); (2) the creek, its canyon and the arroyo cut into it by their bed profiles and cross-sections (water.*); (3) level pads for the places (places.*.pad) and the town's plane (town.ground). Control points are the landform skeleton: the western foothills, the rail bench, the canyon rims, the lower north-east basin, the south-east upland, the southern mesas.

water._doc: Water flows downhill everywhere (the generator checks every bed profile falls). Clean Salt Creek rises in the south-west and passes the Southern Ute community and then the town's south edge before anything else touches it; the town's ditch takes water above town. The mine and Ore Works drain to the dry arroyo, which runs north of town and joins Salt Creek only at the north-east, below the widow's place (valley.md DECIDED: the mines' drainage bypasses town and joins downstream). Creek vertices: [x, z, bed_y, half_width, floor_half, wall_power]: the channel's rim half-width, its flat floor, the wall's curve (1 straight, 1.3 the trestle lab's gorge).

creek.status: DECIDED course (south of town, then to the trestle canyon); PROPOSED line and levels
creek.flow: about 2-4 m wide and ankle to knee deep in a gravel bed (low water); a sandy wash with pools in late summer; cottonwoods and willow only along it

canyon.name: Salt Creek Canyon (the great canyon)
canyon.status: DECIDED shape (deep and narrow at the trestle, carrying on south, widening and shallowing to a passable crossing); PROPOSED line
canyon._doc: The canyon is Salt Creek's own lower course, cut down through the rail bench where the creek drops toward the lower north-east basin. It runs about 520 m south (upstream) from the trestle to its head by Bridge A, shallowing from 27 m to about 3 m, and about 350 m north (downstream) of the trestle before it opens onto the widow's bottomland. Because water runs downhill, the shallow southern end is the UPSTREAM end: the brief's 'more passable farther downstream' is read as 'farther south'.

arroyo.flow: dry most of the year; flash floods after summer storms; steep cut banks 2-5 m; sand and cobble floor

town._doc: The town to Sean's November 7 picture (DECIDED: its arrangement and spacing as drawn, Sean on #467 2026-11-07). Measured off the picture: Main Street's frontage, drawn 1,250 px long, is the DECIDED 250 m, so 5 px a metre along x; x = (picture px - 808) / 5 (808 is the North-South Street's middle). Across (z) the picture is a bird's-eye view, squeezed; its rows are kept in order and given period sizes (lots 125 ft deep, Main Street one surveyor's chain, 66 ft, wide; the rear alleys 20 ft). Lots are reservations ('x0', 'x1' along Main Street); what stands on them comes from the building lab's specs.

ground._doc: The town stands on a gentle slope: down 1.5 m along Main Street's 250 m to the east, and down from the rail bench (+2.8) to the creek bank (-4): about 4 % across, as a creek-side town on its terrace.

main_street.status: DECIDED 250 m; PROPOSED width (66 ft; the old street is 16.8 m)

walks._doc: PROPOSED (#737, waiting on Sean's changes): each building lot's `walk`: `h` its walk's top over the ground at its street edge's middle (m; each owner built his own, so the walks step up and down, the street's fall adding to it); `door` steps (default) or ramp; `w`/`e` its west/east end: steps (default: down to the ground, or to a lower neighbour's walk over a tight gap), ramp, or drop (no steps: jump); `awning` the eave over the walk (m; 0 none); `door_w` the door flight's width; `none` no walk; `why` the reason. Rules: treads of at most `riser_max`, ramps 1 in `ramp_slope`; a walk `rail_at` or more over the dirt has a rail along its street edge (not at its flights or a drop) and from `posts_at` it stands on posts, open underneath.

walk.why: A workshop: the floor kept low so planks and frames slide in off the lumber yard; two treads up. A hoist beam over the doors, no awning.
Stoves and nail kegs lifted off a wagon's tail by a man: knee height. Built first; the store went up beside it, higher.
The loading dock: level with a freight wagon's bed, so barrels and crates roll straight in. Its east end drops 1.1 m into the store alley: jump it, or go round by the steps.
Flour sacks carried in on a shoulder: just high enough to keep the street's dust out of the dough. A barrow ramp up to the butcher's.
Sides of beef carried straight off the wagon bed into the cold room.
